title: silo-proxy-multipath-observability-handoff-for-dedicated-and-private
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Dedicated and Private customers run observability collectors inside their VPCs or on-prem clusters. When we need to route traces/metrics/logs through Redwood infrastructure for aggregation, diagnostics, or replay, current monolithic forwarders create cross-tenant blast radius and make safe failover and partial escalation hard.

Goal: Build a lightweight silo-proxy layer that performs multipath handoff: tenant-aware routing to (a) local collector, (b) isolated Redwood aggregation pipeline, and (c) developer debugging relay. The proxy should preserve trace continuity (trace IDs, parent spans) while enforcing per-tenant isolation, signed envelopes, and adaptive sampling. It must support:
- transparent protocol translation (OTLP/Zipkin/Jaeger/HTTP/HTTPS),
- transactional handoff semantics for replay-safe buffering,
- tenant-bounded backpressure and soft-quota enforcement,
- a configurable failover policy (local -> remote-isolated -> remote-shared),
- debug-only mirroring to a temporarily enabled dev sink without impacting production flow.

Scope: implement proxy binary and routing rules, add tracing hooks to preserve hop provenance, extend console dashboards for multi-path latency/error breakdowns, create rollout plan and runbook for Dedicated and Private customers. Do not change downstream storage schemas in this ticket.

Out of scope: cross-tenant analytics, long-term retention config changes, or marketplace changes for private images.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy binary builds and passes unit tests for OTLP/HTTP ingest formats
End-to-end flow demonstrates a single tenant sending traces that are split to local collector and isolated aggregation with consistent trace IDs and parent/span mapping
Console shows per-path latency percentiles and error rates for at least one pilot Dedicated customer
Backpressure triggers when tenant buffered bytes exceed configured soft quota and logs show correct quota-reason and remediation link
Failover policy correctly reroutes traffic from local to isolated pipeline during simulated local collector outage without trace duplication
Security review completed and keys for envelope signing integrated with KMS in private deployments
Runbook includes steps to disable dev mirroring and to rotate proxy credentials with minimal disruption
implementation_steps: Design: define proxy API surface, routing table format, and envelope schema (with security) - PRD linked in Confluence
Prototype: build Go micro-binary with pluggable adapters for OTLP/Zipkin/HTTP ingestion
Tracing hooks: annotate handoff spans with hop metadata and tenant-hash; ensure KV cache is not leaked in any handoff path
Buffering: implement bounded in-memory ring buffer + disk-backed spill with watermarking and replay-safe sequencing
Backpressure: add per-tenant token-bucket and soft-quota metrics exported to Prometheus
Policy engine: implement simple declarative failover rules and an overrides API for on-call emergencies
Console: add per-tenant multipath dashboard panels (p95 latency by path, error ratio, buffer occupancy)
Testing: chaos simulation to kill local collector, observe failover and replay correctness
Security: integrate KMS envelope signing and add attestation for private/on-prem images
Pilot: enable for 2 Dedicated customers and 1 Private VPC customer; collect metrics for 72h
Rollout: staged canary -> gradual ramp -> GA with migration tool for customers using old forwarder
notes: Related infra ticket: ENG-63214 (onprem sidecar resilience) - we coordinate on auth protocol
Related dashboard spike: PM requested p95-by-path for cost-impact analysis
We must avoid reusing tenant identifiers in logs — use hashed tenant_id across observability layers
Consider using the same envelope signing format as runtime-1.20 for compatibility
Priority of OTLP ingestion first to unblock most customers; Zipkin/legacy adapters follow
Estimate assumes two engineers full-time for 6 weeks plus one reliability engineer for rollout
